title: Anthony the Abbot (17 January)
hookLine: the desert father who heard one Gospel line and walked out; patron of animals, blessed in villages on his day

cards: Two graves are fresh in an Egyptian village, and the young man who buried them was their son. He has land, a younger sister to look after, and a lot on his mind.
One day he walks into church while the Gospel is being read, and the line, his biographer says, lands on him as if it were read for him alone. He walks out and starts giving his fields away.
In some villages, on his feast in January, people still bring cows, horses, dogs and chickens to be blessed in his name.

teach.h: ONE LINE: GO SELL WHAT THOU HAST.
teach.b: Anthony's story comes to us through the Life of Antony, written by Athanasius, the bishop of Alexandria we met yesterday. The line Anthony heard was Jesus speaking to the rich young man in Matthew's Gospel.
In the Douay-Rheims: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor". Anthony did it.
He kept a little back for his sister, Athanasius says, until he heard another line, about not being anxious for tomorrow, and gave that away too.

teach.h: ALONE: TOMBS, THEN AN OLD FORT.
teach.b: He placed his sister with a community of faithful women and went out to live alone: first at the edge of his village, then among old tombs, then deep in the desert, inside an abandoned fort. He stayed a long time.
Athanasius describes a real fight: temptations, fear, nights when he felt attacked. Then the surprise. People came looking for him.
When he finally walked out, Athanasius says, his friends were amazed: he looked neither wasted nor overfed, and his mind was calm.

teach.h: PEOPLE FOLLOW HIM INTO THE DESERT.
teach.b: Others moved into the desert near him to live the same way, and he taught them. That's why tradition calls him the father of monks.
Now the animals. Athanasius tells how wild beasts kept trampling Anthony's little garden.
He caught one gently and told them all, in effect, I do you no harm, so do me none, and leave. And they left. In time, Christians came to call on him as a patron of animals and farm creatures.
So on his day: a priest with holy water in a village square, and a line of farm animals waiting their turn.

how: Catholics keep Saint Anthony the Abbot's memorial in January, and in some places priests bless farm animals and pets on or near his feast.

practice: If there's an animal near you, a dog, a cat, a bird at the window, give it your full attention for a minute and watch how it breathes; if not, bring to mind an animal you've loved. If you pray, give thanks for that creature.
If you don't, just let it be good that it exists.

wordCard.voice: Anthony. The Egyptian abbot who heard one Gospel line, gave his land away, and went to the desert. Others followed, and he became the one tradition calls the father of monks.

orig.note: Greek: Anthony's name as Athanasius wrote it in the Life of Antony.

carryVoice: Your line: the father of monks. He went out alone, and others followed. Day nine hundred fifty-eight.
